newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Volatility trades struck in UK equities.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Volatility trades struck in UK equities.

text.p: Most traders of UK equity options preferred to bide their time on Monday ahead of Wednesday's budget and most of the action was in FTSE 100 index options, dealers said.
One of the larger deals was a volatility trade involving the sale of 1,500 September 4725 calls at between 109p-110p and the purchase of September FTSE futures at 4660.

If properly hedged the direction of FTSE futures will not matter so much for this deal as the effect of volatility on the options. If the market rallies, gains from the futures will be offset by losses from the short options.

Conversely if the market falls, losses from the futures will be made up to some extent by the short calls. But if market volatility falls, this will reduce the call option premium so that the position can be closed at a profit.

More complex was the trade in which a put spread was bought which was hedged by futures. The deal concerned selling 500 July 4525 puts in FTSE at 42p and buying 500 July 4625 puts at 76p against buying September futures at 4660.
It will make money if volatility increases because this will raise the value of the spread. By 1235 GMT, cash FTSE was down 1.0 at 4,639.3 while September futures were down 3.0 at 4,658.0.
There was also a seller of 500 July 4545 puts at 41-1/2p betting that the futures will stay above 4545 by July expiry in order to make a maximum profit of 41-1/2p.

Over in stock options, one large trade was in aero-engine manufacturer Rolls Royce in which 250 August 240 puts were bought at 11p as well as 250 August 260 calls at four pence in a long strangle strategy. Rolls Royce shed two pence to 237p.
For a profit at expiry, the underlying shares need to either be below 225p or above 265p.
